title: Monét Releases Sophomore Album With SZA, Bruno Mars and Bryson Tiller | Entertainment
text:
Monét's sophomore album, released Oct. 2 via Lovett Music and RCA Records, features SZA, Bruno Mars and Bryson Tiller ahead of her Frequency of Love Tour.
Monét released her sophomore studio album on Oct. 2 through Lovett Music and RCA Records, featuring collaborations with SZA, Bruno Mars, Bryson Tiller, Leon Thomas, Chlöe, Lucky Daye and her five-year-old daughter Hazel Monét. Reuniting with longtime producer D’Mile, the 37-year-old singer delivers 22 tracks that explore love in sexual, familial and supernatural contexts.
Monét Reunites With Producer D’Mile
The album was signaled by lead single Let Me, which topped Adult R&B Airplay for three weeks.
A second single, Reach Out, built on the Kaytranada-helmed production of her 2024 song Alright. Both tracks gain vibrancy within the full album, a testament to the sequencing Monét and D’Mile created.
The flirtatious Bryson Tiller-assisted Single flows into the come-hither pulses of Reach Out. Her musings on love lost in the SZA-featuring See You In My Dreams morph into the wedding vow energy of her duet with Bruno Mars, That’s Why I Love You.
Despite a slightly overblown length, the album scoffs at the idea of a sophomore slump, following a three-time Grammy-winning breakthrough record. It engages in constant conversation with both history and the zeitgeist, referencing Brandy’s Almost Doesn’t Count, Dru Hill’s In My Bed, Joe’s All the Things (Your Man Won’t Do) and Bruno Lauzi’s Ritornerai.
Tracklist Explores Love and Black Music
The record’s soundscape mines Black music from gospel to Motown to house, exploring love as a shared experience and an approach to life. In an era that sneers at earnest displays of love, the album fights that head-on.
Persuasion, the last link-up between Victoria and Bryson, was a standout from his 2024 self-titled album, but the new collaboration does not match that bar. Victoria first teased Single during a stop at Hot 97, and its summery hook still sounds flat. Between an uncharacteristically plodding melody and dated production, Single is not the best showcase for either artist.
Victoria goes intergalactic for an interlude, delivering a contemplative cut about waiting for a lover to reach an understanding. The album’s penultimate interlude, a hazy offshoot of I Want You, reimagines pieces of The Beatles’ Michelle, focusing on the I love you refrain and closing with a languid delivery.
A lush intro features regal keys and reverb-drenched horns, with Victoria singing about being tuned to the frequency of love. The tracklist also includes a country-adjacent song, a staple of mid-2020s albums. In another interlude, Victoria uses a darker, femme fatale tone to play a character whose one true love is money.
The beguiling funk of Jaguar made the title track a fan-favorite last era, so Victoria mined similar grounds for Juicy, featuring contributions from D’Mile, Babyface and Michaël Brun. It closes the album’s romance-focused section.
Say Dat serves up the first sliver of spice after smooth opening numbers. Over a sparse, snap-laden beat, Victoria begs her lover to verbalize how much they want, love, need and miss her.
Frequency of Love Tour Dates
Having wrapped her stint as opener for Bruno Mars’ stadium-conquering Romantic Tour, which she joined a month after graduating from culinary school, Monét is preparing for her own headlining trek.
The Frequency of Love Tour will begin at Raleigh’s Red Hat Amphitheater on Oct. 27, visiting major North American cities including New York, Toronto and Nashville, before concluding at San Francisco’s Bill Graham Civic Auditorium on Dec. 17.
